chapter.subject: Science
chapter.chapter: Chapter 5 — Measurement of Length and Motion

excerpts:
[NSEJS 2015 — question paper]
9. A particle moves along the x-axis according to the equation x = 6t where x is displacement 2
in meters and t is time in seconds. Therefore
a) the acceleration of the particle is 6 ms -2
b) the particle follows a parabolic path
c) each second the velocity of the particle changes by 9.8 ms -1
d) the velocity of the particle is 6 ms at t = 0.5 s -1

[INJSO 2013 — question paper]
60. A 100 m sprinter increases her speed from rest uniformly at the rate of 1 m/s upto 2
40 m and covers the remaining distance with uniform speed. The sprinter covers the
first half of the run in t 1 s and the second half in t 2 s. Then:
A. t 1 > t 2
B. t < t 1 2
C. t = t 1 2
D. information given is incomplete.

[INJSO 2011 — question paper]
34. Velocity time graph of four athletes for a given interval of time are as given below. Who has
travelled maximum distance?
a) A b) B c) C d) D

[INJSO 2016 — question paper]
39.
Two projectiles are fired simultaneously from ground level with same initial speed (u). Both
cover same horizontal distance of 160 m on reaching the ground level. One of them reaches 6
sec. prior to the other. Only gravitational acceleration g = 10 m/s governs the motion of both 2
the projectiles. Calculate (u).
[Total = 5 marks]

items.stem: The passage mentions that 1 cm is divided into 10 equal parts. What is the name of the smallest division on a standard 15-cm scale?
What is the standard unit of length in the International System of Units (SI)?
A student measures the length of a table using a 15-cm scale and finds that it is 13.5 cm. Another student measures the same table using a 1-metre scale. What will be the measurement in centimetres?
If a student measures the length of a table using their handspan and finds it to be 13 handspans, what would happen if another student with a different handspan measures the same table?
What does the passage say about the use of body parts for measurement?
If a student uses a 15-cm scale to measure the length of a table and finds it to be 13.5 cm, what would happen if they used a 1-metre scale instead?
If the zero marking on a scale is not clear, how can the length of an object be measured?
If two students measure the same object but from different reference points, what can be said about their measurements?
In which of the following situations is a reference point necessary?
An object is said to be in motion if its position changes with respect to a reference point with time. What is the term used to describe this change in position?
In the given figure, an object is moving along a circular path. What type of motion is this?
A boy walks 200 m in 4 minutes. What is his speed in meters per minute?
A ball is rolling on the ground. It covers 10 cm in the first second, 20 cm in the second second, and 30 cm in the third second. What type of motion is this?
A student measures the length of a leaf using a 15-cm scale as shown in Fig. 5.20. If the scale is aligned as in the figure, what is the length of the leaf?
A ball is moving along a rollercoaster track as shown in Fig. 5.19. Which type of motion does the ball exhibit when it moves from point B to point C?
A student measures the length of a leaf using a 15-cm scale. If the leaf's length is 12 cm and the scale's smallest division is 1 mm, what is the accuracy of the measurement?
A ball is moving along a rollercoaster track. Which type of motion is the ball undergoing when it moves along a straight segment of the track?
Which of the following is an example of linear motion?
In Fig. 5.20, a leaf is being measured using a 15-cm scale. If the length of the leaf is 7.5 cm, what is the total number of divisions on the scale that are covered by the leaf?
A student uses a bicycle to measure the distance between two points. The circumference of the wheel is 1.5 m, and the wheel makes 200 revolutions. How much distance did the student cover?
A student measures the length of a leaf using a scale. The leaf starts at the 2 cm mark and ends at the 9 cm mark on the scale. What is the length of the leaf?
In a children's park, a swing moves back and forth. What type of motion is this?
A pendulum swings back and forth. What can be said about its motion?
If the zero marking on a scale is not clear, how can you still measure the length of an object?
In which of the following cases would the reference point be important for measuring distance?
If a student measures the length of a curved line using a thread and a scale, which of the following is the most important factor to ensure accuracy?
What is the smallest unit of length that can be measured using a 15-cm scale?
If a student measures the length of a table using their handspan, and another student uses a 15-cm scale, which method is more accurate and why?
If a student uses a scale with a broken end, and measures an object from the 1.0 cm mark to the 10.4 cm mark, what is the length of the object?
Which of the following is an example of linear motion?
Which of the following is an example of circular motion?

A student uses a bicycle to measure the distance between two places. He counts 100 sounds from the metal strip attached to the wheel. The circumference of the wheel is 2 m. What is the total distance covered?
Which of the following is the SI unit of length?
A car is moving on a straight road. What type of motion is it exhibiting?
What is the correct way to place the scale while measuring length?
Which of the following is the SI unit of length?
Which of the following is a correct way to measure the length of an object?
What should be the position of the eye while reading the scale?
A child is sitting in a moving bus. From the perspective of the child, are the other passengers in the bus in motion or at rest?
A child observes that the position of the passengers in the bus is not changing with time. What can be concluded about the passengers?
